accepting this costs us the assurance that our actions are likely to succeed, reducing scientific choice to a non-justifiable existential commitment to learn from error rather than to predict success.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If the agent requires a guarantee or even a probabilistic likelihood that the chosen theory will work in the future, this defense fails.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If 'preference' implies an expectation of repeated success based on past performance, this smuggles in induction.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If there exist two theories with identical empirical content and corroboration, this mechanism provides no tie-breaking rule.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "Severe Test Maximization: The mechanism selects the theory that has exposed itself to the greatest risk of falsification (highest empirical content) and survived.
